images.name: American Cocker Spaniel
images.prompt: Create an original, refined naturalistic field-guide portrait, actual native 1536x1024 landscape. One mature adult American Cocker Spaniel, jet black coat with restrained natural highlights, in a relaxed three-quarter standing pose at dog-eye level on short dry meadow grass, muted distant low shrubs and soft overcast morning light. Sturdy compact sporting proportions, gently sloping strong topline, muscular quarters and straight strong forelegs. Breed-accurate refined moderately rounded head, pronounced stop, broad deep short muzzle, full upper lips covering lower jaw, soft dark-brown eyes; long lobular silky low-set ears beginning at the lower eye line. Medium-length flat-to-slightly-wavy silky body coat, moderate chest/ear/leg feathering revealing body lines and paws, never a floor-length skirt or curly wool. Show the complete natural undocked tail anatomically attached at the back line, moderate length tapering from thicker root, proportional feathering, extending at topline or slightly above without curl. Entire body, all four coherent grounded paws, ears and full tail tip fully visible with comfortable crop-safe margins. Subtle painterly realism and tactile fur, elegant restrained landscape, no people, other animals, collar, gear, text, logo or watermark. New composition, not a recreation of a research photograph.

profileEvidence.author: A
profileEvidence.summary: Merry and people-oriented, the American Cocker Spaniel often brings an outgoing warmth to companionship while retaining a keen interest in work. Its sporting roots lie in flushing game from cover; the American breed developed from imported English Cockers and became a separate breed in the mid-twentieth century.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: An outgoing, people-oriented spaniel, the American Cocker often keeps its merry character and willingness to work.

sources.title: United Kennel Club: Cocker Spaniel breed standard
sources.evidence: The History section explicitly distinguishes American from English Cockers, describes early English imports and flushing game, and records separate recognition in1947. Characteristics describes people-oriented, merry temperament and inclination to work; head, ears, body, coat and feet sections define compact sturdy sporting anatomy.

sources.title: Canadian Kennel Club: American Cocker Spaniel
sources.evidence: Temperament describes an outgoing friendly personality; Activity Level notes inclination to work and present companion role. Origin explains development from imported Cockers in North America and eventual separation from English Cocker. Breed-page photograph credited to Nadia Bongelli shows an adult-appearing black American Cocker, rounded but moderate crown, pronounced stop, deep short muzzle with full lips, low-set long silky hanging ears; seated pose does not establish unseen hind feet/tail.

sources.title: Royal Kennel Club: Spaniel (American Cocker) breed standard
sources.evidence: Characteristics describes willingness to work and merry character. Undocked tail section states moderate length, thicker root tapering to tip, proportionate feathering, carried at topline or a little above and never curled over back. Coat section limits feathering so body lines and sporting function remain visible.
